advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the spawn-default test to assert the harness's selected context method directly (e.g. assert type(_worker_context(None))-derived start method == 'spawn') rather than relying on the child's global get_start_method().
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/harness.py:311 `ctx = _worker_context(mp_context)` selects the context; the worker (`_worker_entry`, harness.py:236) runs func in a child whose `multiprocessing.get_start_method()` returns the interpreter global default, not the parent-selected context method
ABSENCE: no assertion ties the observed value to which context object _worker_context returned (e.g. asserting _worker_context(None) is a spawn context, or capturing the context type used to launch)
advisory.finding: test_worker_defaults_to_spawn_context (and the held-out test_default_worker_uses_spawn_while_another_thread_is_live) assert the child's multiprocessing.get_start_method()=='spawn', which reflects the interpreter's GLOBAL default start method rather than the context the harness selected to launch the worker. On a platform whose global default is already spawn, these tests would still pass if the harness reverted its default from get_context('spawn') back to the platform default get_context() — so they do not reliably guard the specific behavior this diff introduces (harness defaulting to the spawn context).
scenarios: A regression that changes the harness default from get_context('spawn') back to get_context() on a Linux runner whose global default is spawn — test still passes
